facts.detail: current_gigabit is derived from OMR data and BDUK delivery data.
future_gigabit indicates future plans reported through OMR data.
bduk_gis indicates whether a premises is included in a Gigabit Infrastructure Subsidy contract.
bduk_gis_contract_scope distinguishes Initial, Deferred and In Procurement premises.
bduk_gis_final_coverage_date is the current final payment date for initial-scope premises, not a guaranteed individual delivery date.

facts.detail: GIS data uses submitted financial models and excludes incidental premises suppliers are not obliged to deliver.
GIS financial-model records undergo multiple assurance levels before inclusion.
Superfast records use contractual Speed and Coverage Templates agreed by suppliers and local authorities.
Voucher records use expected-premises-passed lists for approved projects and BDUK operational assurance.
Gigahub records use BDUK-funded in-scope hub management information and exclude hubs funded by other departments.

facts.detail: Gigabit-contract premises can be added to or removed from initial scope as contracts change.
Approved voucher projects are not contractual and may not deliver every included premises.
Active Superfast contract premises may be descoped and moved into future Gigabit contracts.
Only Gigahubs at least at the assurance stage before build are included.
Approximately 3.7% of premises in interventions are in scope for more than one intervention.

facts.detail: Around 4,900 GIS-contract premises are absent because Ordnance Survey now categorises them as demolished.
Rapid contract changes mean some recent additions or removals may not yet be captured.
Premises connected after the January 2026 OMR may not have current_gigabit set to TRUE.
Not all suppliers respond to BDUK's OMR process, creating coverage gaps.
BDUK says future_gigabit is not directly comparable with Ofcom PND because premises bases, suppliers, evaluation methods and reference dates differ.

guard_streams.source: Closure of the January 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review

facts.detail: The January 2026 National Rolling OMR ran from 6 January to 6 February 2026.
Suppliers were asked for existing and planned gigabit infrastructure over the next three years.
The National Rolling OMR operates every four months in January, May and September.
The process supports strategic planning and prioritisation of procurement Intervention Areas.
OMR data also informs GigaHubs, Gigabit Voucher eligibility and other BDUK interventions.
